claims.statement: A release is a tag plus a GitHub release on the commit shipped; a promotion dev→main records the release line but does not tag — the distinction exists because v0.2.1 shipped untagged and had to be recovered by hand.

release.sh refuses before any mutation unless five preconditions hold: clean tree, HEAD is origin/dev (or --ref), the tag is new locally and on origin, the committed non-blank notes file docs/releases/<version>.md exists, and every workflow on that exact SHA is completed/success.
The version bump is one package.json line, proven by `git diff --numstat` reading `1 1 package.json`, and the annotated tag carries the notes file as its message.

The bump commit is landed through a PR (branch chore/release-v<x>, `gh pr create --base dev`) merged with `--merge`, never a squash, so the tagged commit stays reachable from dev; ruleset 25775908 blocks direct pushes to dev/main.

Before merging the landing PR the script waits for every workflow on the bump commit's own SHA (40 polls × 30s), refusing immediately on any completed non-success, because the ruleset requires a PR but no status checks.
The release is verified as three separate facts: the tag points at local HEAD, origin carries the same tag, and the GitHub release record exists and is published.
After a squash-merged promotion, backmerge.yml opens a `-s ours` bookkeeping PR that restores main as an ancestor of dev; it must be merged with a merge commit.
